newsitem.title: INDIA: India approves 1.68 bln rupee oil terminal plan.
newsitem.headline: India approves 1.68 bln rupee oil terminal plan.

text.p: India on Monday approved a 1.68 billion rupee ($46.9 million) project to modernise a marine oil terminal at Bombay port, the government said in a statement.
It said the expenditure covered a foreign exchange component of 330.1 million rupees, which includes capitalised interest of 112.5 million rupees.

The project will replace old cargo and service lines with new pipelines, construct a new bund and trestle, strengthen existing jetty heads, provide 13 marine unloading arms and replace existing fire fighting facilities.

The project will help reduce pre-berthing congestion of tankers, increasing transfer rates for crude and other products and improving fire-fighting facilities to internationally accepted standards, the statement said.

The overall transfer rate of crude oil will immediately double to 4,250 tonnes per hour and the transfer rate of other products will swiftly multiply to 1,650 tonnes per hour from about 340 tonnes per hour at present.
